newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador Congress says $100 mln oil revenues lost.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador Congress says $100 mln oil revenues lost.

text.p: An Ecuadorean Congress committee investigating corruption said Monday the country had lost about $100 million of oil income through irregularities in state oil contracts.

Oil is Ecuador's main foreign currency earner and the new government of President Fabian Alarcon has denounced dealings in the oil industry during the government of Abdala Bucaram, who was ousted in February for "mental incompetence."

Napoleon Saltos, head of Congress's Watchdog Committee, alledged that Bucaram government officials were responsible for the losses. He named former Energy Minister Alfredo Adum and the former head of state oil firm Petroecuador, Patricio Lopez.
"We have analyzed about 100 contracts and given priority to five or six, where there is clear evidence of the losses," Saltos told reporters.

He estimated that the country had lost $1.49 a barrel in crude oil export contract irregularities, for which he said parliament and the Supreme Court would have to take punitive action against the relevant former officials.
"Responsibility lies with those who were in charge of energy policy, which means former minister Adum and the man who was in charge of Petroecuador -- Lopez," he said.

The new president of Petroecuador, Rafael Almeida, said a month ago he would investigate recent contracts for signs of corruption. The company produces more than 80 percent of the country's hydrocarbon output of 390,000 bdp.
Congress expelled 13 deputies for alleged corruption last week on the Watchdog Committee's recommendation. The Supreme Court ordered their arrest this weekend.
